bull.b: Exceptional TPV growth combined with strong retention shows that DLocal is expanding existing merchant relationships, not relying only on new customer wins. Broader use across countries, payment methods and products can support durable volume growth and deepen the platform’s role in merchant payment flows.

Expanded licensing and regulatory coverage strengthens DLocal’s ability to operate across emerging markets and add local payment capabilities. This infrastructure can raise execution barriers for competitors, support merchant confidence, and provide a foundation for continued geographic and product expansion.

Robust recent operating and free cash flow, closely aligned with earnings, indicates solid cash conversion and supports self-funded investment in technology, licensing and market expansion. This financial capacity also gives DLocal flexibility to pursue growth while maintaining capital returns.

bear.b: The sustained decline in gross and net margins indicates that rapid growth has not translated proportionally into profitability. Continued compression could limit operating leverage, reduce the cash generated per dollar of TPV, and make future earnings more sensitive to pricing and processing-cost changes.

Lower take rates and elevated processing costs can weaken monetization even when transaction volume grows strongly. Mexico demonstrates how merchant mix, pricing tiers and local payment economics may constrain gross-profit expansion, creating an ongoing challenge for converting scale into durable margin improvement.

Although recent cash generation is strong, the prior period of negative operating and free cash flow shows that working-capital or timing effects can materially affect reported cash conversion. Rising leverage also reduces the company’s previously net-cash-like flexibility as the business scales.
